strengths: Well-motivated technical contribution identifying and addressing the re-masking problem in mask-absorbing discrete diffusion models through clever use of star-shaped noise process
Solid theoretical framework with Theorem 3.1 providing KL divergence upper bounds and Lemma 3.2 elegantly decomposing objectives into interpretable prior and likelihood terms

Comprehensive experimental validation with effective ablation study (Section 4.3) demonstrating importance of star-shaped noise, detailed hyperparameter specifications, and GPU memory efficiency advantages (4.7 GiB vs 20.9 GiB)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (especially Figure 2 demonstrating early structure determination) and thorough appendix enabling reproducibility
Demonstrates extensibility to motion data through masked generative models, showing broader applicability beyond images
weaknesses: No empirical performance advantage over existing methods—performs comparably or worse than continuous baselines (DDRM: 24.00 PSNR vs G2D2: 23.20 on ImageNet SR; DDRM: 27.30 vs G2D2: 22.71 on deblurring), undermining the main contribution
Weak motivation for using discrete diffusion models for images specifically; paper emphasizes success in other modalities but fails to establish why practitioners should prefer this over DPS/DDRM
Computational cost is high (194s vs DDRM's 4s) substantially negating memory efficiency gains; unclear practical scenario where computational overhead is justified

Motion experiments are underdeveloped with only qualitative results (Figure 14), no quantitative evaluation, and no comparison with continuous latent space methods (Song et al. 2023b; Uchida et al. 2024)

Significant approximation in theory (substituting learned prior p̃θ for true conditional q(z₀|zₜ) in Eq. 7) is not thoroughly analyzed; sensitivity to this approximation and impact on final distribution quality unclear
Small experimental scale (100 images per dataset) without error bars; different pre-trained models for different baselines makes comparisons potentially unfair and results difficult to interpret
Numerous hyperparameters requiring task-specific tuning (Table 3) with complex learning rate/KL scheduling; limited sensitivity analysis beyond forget coefficient reduces reproducibility confidence
Limited engagement with concurrent discrete diffusion guidance methods (Chen et al. 2024b, Li et al. 2024, Nisonoff et al. 2024); unclear positioning relative to existing training-free approaches

strengths: First training-free method for solving image inverse problems using discrete diffusion models, addressing a genuine gap in the literature
Well-motivated identification of mask-absorbing discrete diffusion's fundamental limitation (early decisions cannot be corrected), with clear demonstration in Figure 2
Theoretically grounded framework with Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 3.2 providing principled KL divergence bounds and variational justification
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including ablation studies demonstrating the value of star-shaped noise (significant improvement over Markov variant)
Honest acknowledgement of limitations and detailed reproducibility information with extensive appendices
Extension to motion generation demonstrates broader applicability beyond images
weaknesses: No practical performance advantage over baselines: G2D2 achieves comparable or worse results than PSLD, DDRM, and ReSample across tasks (e.g., LPIPS 0.349 vs PSLD 0.332 on ImageNet SR), failing to justify the added complexity
Significant computational overhead: G2D2 requires 194 seconds vs DDRM's 4 seconds (50x slower) with only marginal memory savings, undermining practical utility

Theoretical substitution of q(z₀|zₜ) with p̃θ(z₀|zₜ) is heuristic and inadequately justified; prior is trained on Markov process but applied to star-shaped process with no quantification of this mismatch
Gumbel-Softmax continuous relaxation error is unanalyzed and unquantified; no ablation on temperature parameter or sensitivity studies despite this being a key differentiability mechanism
Limited experimental scope: only 100 images per dataset, no statistical significance testing, purely qualitative motion experiments without metrics, single discrete diffusion model tested
Extensive task-specific hyperparameter tuning required (Table 3) with dataset-dependent settings and dynamic scheduling of learning rates/KL coefficients; most design choices lack ablation studies
Incremental novelty: combines existing techniques (star-shaped noise from Okhotin et al. 2024, Gumbel-Softmax, standard variational inference) without clear conceptual advance
Critical gap unanswered: the paper explicitly states it does not surpass continuous baselines yet provides no compelling argument for when or why practitioners should use this more complex method

strengths: Novel application filling a genuine gap: first training-free inverse problem solving approach using discrete diffusion models with practical applicability to domains like motion generation
Rigorous theoretical foundation: Theorem 3.1 provides principled KL divergence bounds, and the star-shaped noise process is well-motivated theoretically
Clear problem diagnosis with effective visualization: Figure 2 convincingly shows the mask-absorbing limitation, and the proposed re-masking solution via star-shaped noise is natural
Comprehensive experimental validation including ablation study (Section 4.3) demonstrating the necessity of the star-shaped noise, multiple datasets/tasks, and application to motion data
Strong implementation clarity with detailed Algorithm 1, extensive appendix specifications, and hyperparameter tables enabling reproducibility
Well-written presentation with effective visualizations and clear narrative structure
weaknesses: Limited practical improvements: G2D2 achieves comparable but not superior performance compared to continuous methods (e.g., FFHQ SR: 0.271 LPIPS vs DPS 0.227), undermining practical motivation despite increased complexity

Confounded experimental comparison: Different pre-trained models used for each method makes it difficult to isolate method contribution; VQ-Diffusion prior appears weaker than pixel-domain models, especially on FFHQ

No computational efficiency gains despite theoretical hope: 194s vs DPS 277s (slower gradient-based baseline) and DDRM 4s; modest memory advantage (4.7 GiB); optimization overhead (30 iterations/step) unexplored

Incremental algorithmic novelty: Star-shaped noise from Okhotin et al./Zhang et al., Gumbel-Softmax standard, variational factorization common; main contribution is combination rather than fundamentally new techniques

Limited experimental scope: Only 256×256 resolution (scalability unclear), small evaluation sets (100 images), motion experiments purely qualitative without metrics, minimal hyperparameter sensitivity analysis

Theoretical approximation under-analyzed: Substitution of p̃_θ(z_0|z_t) for q(z_0|z_t) is key approximation but no empirical analysis of error magnitude or impact on results; fixed Gumbel temperature lacks sensitivity study
Insufficient quantification of re-masking benefit: While ablation shows improvement, diagnostic analysis of how much re-masking vs. other factors contribute is limited
Overclaiming of novelty: Repeated 'first approach' framing and positioning as major contribution somewhat oversell the incremental nature of combining existing techniques

strengths: Well-motivated problem identifying practical limitations of discrete diffusion for inverse problems with clear solutions proposed
Solid theoretical framework with formal justification (Theorems 3.1, Lemma 3.1) for the optimization objective and star-decomposed distribution
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with proper ablations (star-shaped vs Markov noise clearly shows ~10% improvement) across multiple datasets and baselines
Significant practical benefits demonstrated: 77% GPU memory reduction (4.7 vs 20.9 GiB for PSLD) enabling inference on consumer 8 GiB GPUs
Excellent supplementary material with detailed hyperparameters, failure mode analysis, and honest discussion of limitations
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figure 3 on graphical models is particularly well-done)
Training-free applicability demonstrated across domains (images and motion) without additional training
weaknesses: Limited originality: star-shaped processes recently proposed by others (Okhotin et al. 2024, Zhang et al. 2024); paper primarily combines existing techniques
Performance is comparable to, not superior than, continuous methods (within 0.02-0.05 LPIPS difference), undermining methodological advancement claims
Critical approximation not analyzed: substituting trained prior p̃_θ(z0|zt) for true posterior q_star(z0|zt) lacks quality quantification; impact on convergence guarantees unexplored
Convergence properties unclear: only 30 optimization iterations per timestep with no formal convergence analysis; forgetting coefficient γ appears ad-hoc
Inconsistent baseline comparisons: different pre-trained models used for different methods (acknowledged but problematic for fair comparison)
Computational speed trade-off: 194s per image is slower than DDRM (4s) and comparable to PSLD, limiting practical advantage
Limited scope: restricted to linear inverse problems and mask-absorbing discrete diffusion; generalization unclear
Hyperparameter sensitivity: different settings required per dataset (Table 4), raising reproducibility and generalization concerns
Motion experiments show limitations: Table 3 demonstrates underperformance versus OmniControl/GMD on trajectory and location errors despite good FID
Missing code URL in paper; some implementation details relegated to appendix

strengths: Addresses relevant problem of extending inverse problem solving to discrete diffusion models
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple datasets, tasks, and extensive ablations
Significant GPU memory efficiency (77% reduction: 4.7 GiB vs 20.9 GiB for PSLD)
Solid theoretical framework with formal justification (Theorem 3.1, Lemma 3.1) for variational approximation
Well-written presentation with good motivation and intuitive illustrations (e.g., Figure 2 on mask-absorbing limitations)
Clear demonstration of extensibility to masked generative models beyond discrete diffusion
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: star-shaped process from prior work (Okhotin et al. 2024), Gumbel-Softmax is standard; main contribution is combining existing techniques

Inconsistent and modest empirical results: performance degradation vs baselines (e.g., ImageNet SR: 0.340 vs 0.331 LPIPS for PSLD; FFHQ SR: 0.265 vs 0.238 for DPS); only advantage is memory, not quality

Star-decomposed distribution (Eq. 5) introduces substantial approximation (ignores z_{t+1:T} dependencies) whose practical impact is never quantified; justification beyond computational convenience unclear
No experimental comparison to recent discrete diffusion guidance methods (Nisonoff et al. 2024, Li et al. 2024, Chen et al. 2024b, Feynman-Kac steering) despite mentioning them
Severe hyperparameter complexity without systematic sensitivity analysis: multiple scheduling parameters, task-specific tuning required (Table 4), only one ablation on forget coefficient
Approximation error from Gumbel-Softmax relaxation never quantified; substitution of p_θ(z_0|z_t) for q_star(z_0|z_t) assumes prior network transfers but never validated
Weak robustness: Figure 9 shows failures when prompts mismatch target; E.7 shows text conditioning benefits vary inconsistently across datasets
Limited scope: only linear inverse problems, only VQ-VAE based models; authors acknowledge specialization but significantly restricts impact
Computational efficiency incompletely addressed: runtime comparable to DPS (194s vs 277s), requires 30 optimization iterations per timestep; advantage is primarily memory, not speed
Theorem 3.1 provides only loose KL bound without practical guidance; no convergence guarantees for optimization procedure; variational approximation quality never analyzed in practice
Underdeveloped motion application: Table 3 shows worse trajectory/location errors than baselines without explanation; weak conclusion ('shows promise')
Reproducibility concerns: code link missing, complex hyperparameter scheduling scattered across appendices, many task-specific parameters make independent reproduction difficult

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine gap between discrete and continuous diffusion for inverse problems
Solid theoretical contributions: star-decomposed distribution elegantly maintains desired marginal while reducing complexity; Theorems 3.1 and Lemma 3.1 provide rigorous justification
Technically sound approach appropriately combining star-shaped noise process with variational inference and Gumbel-Softmax relaxation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (ImageNet, FFHQ), tasks (SR, deblurring, motion), and baselines with meaningful ablation study (Section 4.3)
Significant practical benefit: 77% GPU memory reduction (4.7 vs 20.9 GiB) enabling inference on consumer hardware
Extensive supplementary evaluation including text conditioning effects, prior selection impact, failure mode analysis, and additional metrics
Strong reproducibility commitment with promised code release, detailed hyperparameters, and comprehensive implementation details
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: star-shaped noise (Okhotin et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2024) and Gumbel-Softmax are existing techniques; contribution is primarily their combination
No quality improvements over baselines: G2D2 achieves 0.340 LPIPS on ImageNet SR vs 0.331 for PSLD, 0.351 for DDRM; FID/KID often worse (Tables 8-11)
Computational speed not improved: 194 seconds per image is slower than several baselines (DPS 277s, though both slow)
Approximation quality not validated empirically: qstar-decomp(z0:T|y) ≠ qstar(z0:T|y) per Property 3; impact of sampling from decomposed joint on solution quality unexplored
Significant hyperparameter complexity: dataset/task-specific settings (Table 4) with minimal ablation studies; learning rate and KL scheduling appear ad-hoc
Text conditioning dependency: Figure 9 shows failure modes when prompts mismatch ground truth; limited solutions proposed
Motion experiments show substantial gaps in trajectory (0.272 vs 0.053) and location errors (0.116 vs 0.015) compared to OmniControl
Missing comparisons: Feynman-Kac steering (Singhal et al., 2025) mentioned but not compared; limited comparison with other discrete guidance methods
Limited experimental scope: only linear inverse problems, only images/motion (not audio/video), only 256×256 resolution
Gumbel-Softmax temperature fixed at 1.0 with no ablation study on this critical hyperparameter
